nodes.title: MCG-finite representations
nodes.statement: For an oriented connected finite-type surface S=Σ(g,n), a rank-r complex representation ρ is MCG-finite when its actual GL_r(C)-conjugacy class has finite orbit under orientation-preserving mapping classes acting through Out(π₁S). Use pure mapping classes for ordered punctures; full versus pure finiteness is equivalent because their index is finite. No semisimplification is taken.
proofSteps: Use conjugacy of homomorphisms as an equivalence relation; precomposition by an inner automorphism induces conjugation by ρ of that element.
Descend the outer action to classes; identify finite orbits with finite-index stabilizers.
acceptance: Establish the stated result with the listed hypotheses; preserve base-point and conjugation conventions.

nodes.title: Versal family fundamental groups
nodes.statement: For a punctured étale-versal hyperbolic family and compatible basepoints, 1→π₁(C°_m)→π₁(C°)→π₁(M)→1 is exact; the map π₁(M)→PMod(g,n) has finite-index image. Consequently the outer monodromy on the fibre is the restriction of the mapping-class action.

nodes.title: Finite-orbit operations
nodes.statement: Finite direct sums, tensor products and duals of MCG-finite representations are MCG-finite. Every irreducible constituent of the semisimplification is MCG-finite. A subrepresentation or quotient singled out functorially under all representation isomorphisms is MCG-finite, including the socle and its quotient. Arbitrary non-characteristic subquotients of a nonsplit representation are not asserted to have finite orbit.
proofSteps: Intersect finitely many stabilizers for sums and tensors; transport duals.
Mapping classes permute the finite set of semisimple constituents. Isomorphism-invariant submodules and quotients transport under each stabilizing intertwiner.

nodes.title: Rank-one canonical finiteness
nodes.statement: For g≥1 and n≥0 every MCG-finite character π₁Σ(g,n)→C× has finite image. In particular every positive-rank MCG-finite representation has finite determinant.
proofSteps: Use powers of nonseparating Dehn twists in the stabilizer to force torsion values on simple generators; use the puncture relations and the rank-one finite-orbit classification cited there.

nodes.title: Canonical projective extension
nodes.statement: Let ρ:N→GL_r(C), r>0, be irreducible, with N the hyperbolic surface point-pushing group. Let Γ be the finite-index pure mapping-class stabilizer of [ρ] and Γ̃ its preimage in PMod(g,n+1). For γ∈Γ̃ select an actual GL intertwiner Aγ from ρ to ρ∘conjγ. Its class defines a homomorphism ρ̂:Γ̃→PGL_r(C) restricting to Pρ. Uniqueness is within the class of extensions represented by these actual intertwiners, not among arbitrary PGL extensions.
proofSteps: Schur makes the space of actual intertwiners one dimensional; multiplication is compatible modulo scalars.
Inner elements act by the class of ρ. Pull back to a fine level scheme to obtain a projective local system on a versal total space.
acceptance: Establish the stated result with the listed hypotheses; preserve base-point and conjugation conventions.

nodes.title: Fibre-prescribed linear lifting
nodes.statement: For g≥1, start with the projective family extension of an irreducible MCG-finite ρ with finite determinant. After connected dominant étale base change it lifts to an actual GL_r(C) representation of the total-space group with finite determinant, whose restriction is isomorphic to the original ρ, not just projectively isomorphic.
proofSteps: Set D=detρ(N) and use the central isogeny det⁻¹(D)→PGL_r with finite kernel μ (r>0). The obstruction restricts to zero on N.
Use discrete LHS filtration: first kill the component in H¹(Q,H¹(N,μ)) after making its finite module constant; only then kill the newly determined inflated class in H²(Q,μ).
Compare the resulting fibre lift with ρ. Make the finite mismatch character invariant, kill its transgression in H²(Q,μ), extend it to the total group, and twist the lift.

nodes.title: Irreducible normal restriction
nodes.statement: For arbitrary groups G and N normal in G, let ρ:G→GL_r(C) have finite determinant and irreducible restriction to N. If ρ(N) is finite then ρ(G) is finite; if ρ|N is unitarizable then ρ is unitarizable. No finiteness of G or finite index of N is assumed.
proofSteps: For a finite N-image, the kernel of conjugation on that image centralizes an irreducible representation and hence consists of scalars; finite determinant bounds these scalars.
An N-invariant positive Hermitian form is unique up to positive scalar. Each G element transports it to such a multiple; finite determinant forces that multiple to be one.

nodes.title: Relative unitary decomposition
nodes.statement: Let A be a local Artinian C-algebra with residue C and V a local system of finite free A-modules on a punctured étale-versal family with g≥1. Suppose the restriction to a chosen fibre is isomorphic over A to U⊗C A with U unitary. After dominant étale base change, V≃⊕ᵢ(Uᵢ⊗C π°^*Wᵢ), where Uᵢ are total-space unitary complex local systems with pairwise nonisomorphic irreducible fibre restrictions and Wᵢ are finite free A-local systems on M. This is fibre-constant deformation, not merely unitary reduction mod m_A.
proofSteps: Extend the irreducible constituents of U by linear realization, and use the normal-restriction theorem to make them unitary on the total space.
Define Wᵢ=π°_*Hom(Uᵢ,V); Schur and fibrewise evaluation give finite freeness and the displayed decomposition.
acceptance: Establish the stated result with the listed hypotheses; preserve base-point and conjugation conventions.

nodes.title: Higher Prym actions
nodes.statement: For a surjection φ:π₁Σ(g,b,p)↠H onto a finite group, put K=kerφ and let Γ⊂PMod(g,b,p+1) stabilize φ up to inner conjugacy in H. Restriction of the based automorphism to K acts on H¹(K,C), with the inverse-pullback convention giving a left action, and on H₁(K,C). It also acts on V_K=H₁ of the compactified covering surface. For each irreducible H-module σ, take the full σ-isotypic subspace σ⊗Hom_H(σ,V), embedded by evaluation; do this separately for open cohomology and compact homology. Γ normalizes the H-action up to inner automorphism, so the isotypic subspaces are stable.
proofSteps: Import the actual covering attached to K and its deck action, and the supplied singular homology/cohomology.
Use functoriality for based automorphisms preserving K, fill ends for the compact quotient, and use the generic semisimple isotypic projector.

Also supply curve-chain normalization and algebraic descent of invertible intertwiners. The current general formal-comparison stage does not assert all these character-variety contracts; propose a representation-moduli extension in the same owner.

Supply a smooth projective SNC compactification preserving the given quasiprojective open after finite level cover and normalization, with a boundary-inertia computation under the chosen resolution. The current resolution theorem supplies smooth SNC compactification; the additional compatibility that exceptional meridians map to products of twist powers must be proved using the pointed stable-boundary charts.

Use finite-determinant reductive monodromy nonabelian Hodge theory, including LL24 Theorem 4.3.1 from Mochizuki Theorem 10.5 with constant determinant and reductive-preserving input. Export a verified bridge to an actual connected algebraic fixed-determinant family linking the original and a fibre-unitary representation, or an alternative proof sufficient for LL24 Theorem 8.5.3. A continuous path in a Betti moduli space does not by itself meet Lemma 8.5.2.

Use polarizable complex variations, admissible graded-polarizable real mixed variations, canonical logarithmic extensions, fixed part, and regular-singular Riemann–Hilbert/canonical mild models. Specifically R¹π°_* of a unitary local system has real MHS weights 1 and 2 with W₁=R¹π_*j_*V and F¹ from E⊗ω(D). The rational/integral mixed-Hodge carrier at the pins does not cover arbitrary real unitary coefficients. Import generic variation definitions, not another carrier here.

Supply exactly LL24 Theorem 1.7.1 (rank of each nonzero sublocal system ≥2g−2rk V for total-space unitary V) and Theorem 6.2.1 (H⁰(M,R¹π°_*V)=0 for finite-free local Artin C coefficients, fibre-constant unitary deformation, rank_A V<g). Also supply LL22 Theorem 1.2.12 with an isomonodromic deformation to an analytically general fibre and rank<2√(g+1). These are not arbitrary-subquotient bounds or unitarity of a PVHS on any single curve. For Artinian decomposition import only C.0–C.2 of this roadmap, never its final finiteness layers.

Supply strong adjoint H¹ rigidity, its implication to middle-extension rigidity after quasi-unipotence, finite-determinant strongly rigid semisimple→complex PVHS, and KP20 Theorem 1.2 for split connected reductive Z-groups with G-irreducibility, middle-extension adjoint rigidity, finite abelianization and quasi-unipotent boundary. Include G-valued companions, not just GL integrality. Resolve the precise integral-Hodge-realization versus geometric-origin formulation in LL24 Corollary 9.1.4: track complex direct summands, an ambient integral lattice and all coefficient embeddings; never demand a rank-r Z-lattice on an arbitrary complex constituent. Supply geometric-origin descent to arithmeticity for the residual application and the separate physical-rigidity examples.

gaps.title: Artin good-neighbourhood comparison

gaps.title: Hodge-engine supplier coverage

gaps.title: Nonabelian Hodge algebraic-family bridge
gaps.detail: Read LL24 pp.27 and43. The deformation statement and the connected algebraic-family constancy lemma have different hypotheses. Verify these generic GIT statements and the fixed-determinant Hodge path in the suppliers. Until then the semisimple and general finiteness proofs remain conditional on that contract.

gaps.title: Boundary resolution compatibility
gaps.detail: A normalization of a level compactification need not be smooth or have simple normal crossings. Import resolution preserving the open and prove its new inertia loops remain commuting twist products before applying KP20. AS16 Proposition 2.4 itself was read directly.

gaps.title: Hurwitz existence primary-source check

gaps.title: Generic étale family exactness and Riemann existence

gaps.title: Integral PVHS and geometric-origin semantics
gaps.detail: The literal reading that every complex finite-image constituent itself carries an integral lattice is false. gaps.detail: The actual representation scheme, fixed-determinant connected family, semisimple closed-orbit criterion and GIT closed-locus descent need named targets in the moduli owner. R09.6 is the request anchor and does not yet provide these statements.

gaps.detail: The geometric residual surjection is not a specified residual representation of a fixed arithmetic group. Supply that extension, continuity/representability hypotheses and the finite-coefficient-point theorem before deriving nonflatness. No complete-intersection claim is planned.

gaps.title: Augmentation nonsplitting computation

gaps.title: Morita integral normalization
gaps.detail: Morita 1989 Proposition 6.4 was not read. Its restriction may be a nonprimitive multiple of the abelianization cocycle; verify the multiple and separate integral and rational extension claims.

gaps.title: Rank-two classifications
